$$

Given that the differential equation

$$

feedback.worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

To find the complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by

$$
{y}_{c}^{′}+3{y}_{c}=0.
$$

Solving this equation, we find that the complementary solution is

$$
{y}_{c}=A{e}^{-3x}
$$

where $A$ is an arbitrary constant.

We now need to find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $13\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).$ So, we assume the particular solution to be 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants to be determined. 

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}=-2\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+2\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).
$$

To find the values of $\alpha ,$ and $\beta ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
(-2\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+2\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))+3(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))=13\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(2\beta +3\alpha )\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+(-2\alpha +3\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)=13\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2\beta +3\alpha =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)) \\ -2\alpha +3\beta =13\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x))\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-2,\beta =3.$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=A{e}^{-3x}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).
$$

Now, we can find the constant $A$ using the initial conditions.

Substituting $y(0)=1$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A{e}^{-3\cdot 0}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0)+3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot 0) & =1 \\ A-2-0 & =1 \\ A & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=3{e}^{-3x}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).
$$
